Description: no cost. these are on hand
metal gear servo. 55g, 25t spline. i measured mine at 39.9 x 19.7 x 42.9mm
Why I need it: the only thing in the build that moves. it tilts the pan and the item slides off one side or the other
Notes: Measured mine with calipers. Body is 39.9mm not the spec 40.7 and the shaft sits 10.95mm off centre. The CAD is built to my unit

Description: the round disc that clamps onto the servo spline. the printed hub bolts to this
Why I need it: a 25t spline has 0.74mm teeth. no printer i have access to can resolve that, so the horn is the only thing that can actually grip the shaft
Notes: Ships in the bag with the MG996R

Description: SUBTOTAL
the funding request
my custom hat. 2 layer, 65 x 45mm, 1.6mm fr4
Why I need it: everything between the pi and the mechanism lives on this board - the load cell amp, the mosfet, all of it

Description: npn pass transistor that makes the hx711's analog supply. sot-23
Why I need it: makes the clean analog supply that excites the load cell bridge. feed the bridge off the noisy rail and the weight reading wanders

Description: logic-level n-channel mosfet. sot-23
Why I need it: switches the led ring. a pi gpio can't drive it directly

Description: assorted 1% 0805 resistors. ten values used on the board
Why I need it: ten resistors spread across the board - dividers, current limits, pullups and the 0r star ground link

Description: 0805 ceramic caps for decoupling and filtering
Why I need it: every ic needs decoupling right at its pins or it browns itself out on its own switching noise
Notes: C1 C2 C3 C5 C6 C8

Description: bulk cap that sits at the servo connector. 8mm radial
Why I need it: the servo yanks current in spikes. without bulk sitting right at the connector that spike turns into a brownout
Notes: Mount at the connector NOT at the regulator. The trace between them is what turns a spike into a brownout

Description: the 2x20 female socket for j1 plus 1x02 x4, 1x03 x2, 1x04 x1
Why I need it: everything off-board plugs in here - load cell, servo, led ring and break-beam. the 2x20 socket is how the hat sits on the pi
Notes: Covers all eight connectors including the 2x20 female socket the HAT sits on

Description: 8mp fixed focus camera. shoots the item top down
Why I need it: takes the photo the classifier runs on. fixed focus is fine because the camera and the pan never move relative to each other
Notes: Ships with the 22-pin Zero cable. Mount is not modelled in CAD yet

Description: strain gauge bar that weighs the item. 80 x 12.7 x 12.7mm
Why I need it: weight catches what a photo can't. a full drink and an empty can look identical to a camera
Notes: Buy the CELL ONLY. Kits bundle an HX711 module you do not need - the HAT already has one, and those modules run at 5V not 3.3V

Description: 5v white ring that lights the pan. 60mm outer, 44mm inner
Why I need it: so every photo the classifier sees is lit the same way. light inside a bin varies wildly and the model shouldn't have to cope with that
Notes: Retainer is not modelled in CAD yet MUST be 5V - J7 pin 1 is fed from the +5V rail. A 12V ring will not light

Description: emitter and receiver across the throat. 5mm barrel
Why I need it: the trigger for everything. without it the pi has no idea something arrived

Description: skateboard bearing the pan turns on. 22 od x 8 id x 7 w
Why I need it: carries the free end of the pan. without it the whole pan hangs off the servo shaft and the gearbox takes the load

Description: makes the servo's own 5-6v rail. 3a minimum
Why I need it: the servo gets its own supply. share a regulator with the pi and a stalling servo browns out the pi and corrupts the sd card
Notes: Must NOT share a regulator with the Pi. The two grounds meet at exactly one 0R link on the board. MG996R pulls about 2.5A stalled so anything under 3A will brown out

Item: M2.5, M3, M4 screws and nuts
Description: the fasteners that hold the mechanism together
Why I need it: holds the mechanism together - idler to pan, brackets to the base plate, pi to its mount

Description: holds the hat off the pi so the two boards can't short
Why I need it: keeps the hat off the pi so nothing on either board touches the other

Description: 24-bit bridge adc. sop-16, sits on the hat
Why I need it: reads the load cell. a bare strain gauge puts out microvolts and nothing else in the build can see a signal that small
Notes: Buy the bare SOP-16 chip. It goes ON the HAT. Do NOT buy an HX711 breakout module

Item: USB C Female to Micro USB Male Adapter
Description: lets my pi 4b supply plug into the zero. usb-c one end, micro usb the other
Why I need it: so i can use the pi 4b supply i already own instead of buying another one. the 4b supply is usb-c with a fixed cable and the zero takes micro usb
Notes: Saves buying a second power supply. Plug into the port marked PWR IN, not the OTG one next to it

Description: the pi's only storage. a1 rated so it loads the model quick enough
Why I need it: the pi has no storage of its own. it won't boot without one
Notes: A1 rated so random reads are quick enough to load the model

Description: the brain. 512mb, runs the whole sort loop
Why I need it: runs the whole loop - trigger, capture, classify, tilt, log. i picked it over a 4b because it idles at 0.4w instead of 2.7w and this thing can never sleep between items
Notes: Bought bare instead of a starter kit
